facts: The appellants are owners of the lands in Plot No. 16 of an extent of 5 bighas, 6 biswas and 14 biswas respectively in Village Bairam Nagar, Pargana Nahtaur, Tahsil Dhampur, District Bijnore.

These lands along with other lands were notified by publication in the State Gazette under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act') on 23 July 1983 and the declaration under Section 6 was also published simultaneously dispensing with the inquiry under Section 5-A.

The appellants challenged the validity of the notification under Section 4(1) and the exercise of the power given under Section 17(1) read with Section 17(4) dispensing with the inquiry under Section 5-A.
issues: Whether the Government would be justified in depending with the inquiry under Section 5-A
Whether the right to shelter is a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(e) and it is a facet of inseparable meaningful right to life under Article 21
petitioner_arguments: The proposal was put up in 1979 and the notification was approved in February but published on 30 April 1983 which would show that the urgency is not such which does not brook the delay of 30 days in conducting inquiry under Section 5-A.

In all the acquisitions for housing purpose conducting inquiry under Section 5-A should be the rule and dispensing with such inquiry should be exceptional and only in rare cases like those covered by Section 17(2).

The right to conduct an inquiry under Section 5-A is a valuable right and minimal safeguard to the owner and it would not be abrogated by exercising power of invoking urgency clause under Section 17(4) of the Act.
respondent_arguments: It forms the opinion of urgency to take immediate possession for the said purpose.
The State Government is statutorily empowered to exercise the power under Section 17(4).

When the Government forms an opinion that it is necessary to require immediate possession of the land for building houses for the Dalits, it forms the opinion of urgency to take immediate possession for the said purpose.
court_reasoning: The opinion of urgency formed by the appropriate Government to take immediate possession, is a subjective conclusion based on the material before it and it is entitled to great weight unless it is vitiated by mala fides or colourable exercise of power.
The right to shelter is not a constitutionally guaranteed right.
Right to social and economic justice conjointly commingles with right to shelter as an inseparable component for meaningful right to life.
holding: The State parties will take appropriate steps to ensure realisation of this right.
The right to residence and settlement is a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(e) and it is a facet of inseparable meaningful right to life under Article 21.
The deprivation, therefore, must be consistent with the procedure established by law.
